title: Telemetry decoder and schema reconciliation pipeline
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Incoming usage telemetry has grown more diverse (mobile SDK, edge collectors, server-side proxies). We currently reject or drop messages when minor schema drift occurs, which leads to noisy alerts and lost signal. Goal: implement a decoder + reconciliation pipeline that can safely parse heterogeneous events, apply best-effort normalization, and surface lightweight validation failures to the Console without dropping usable fields. The pipeline should preserve provenance, be idempotent, and support gradual schema evolution without manual migrations.

Scope: build a new stateless 'decoder' service that consumes raw messages from the central Kafka topic (usage-events-raw), normalizes envelope fields (timestamp, customer_id, route_id), consults a centralized schema registry for validation rules, attempts auto-reconciliation for safe drift (renaming, string->enum soft coercion, numeric parsing), and forwards canonicalized events to usage-events-canonical or to a quarantine topic for manual inspection. Include metrics, tracing, and an operator UI for sampling quarantined events.

Out of scope: full schema-free ingestion of arbitrary payloads; replacing existing producer-side validation; long-term storage schema migrations.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Decoder service deployed to staging consuming from usage-events-raw and writing to usage-events-canonical and usage-events-quarantine as appropriate.
2) End-to-end tests cover at least 8 common drift scenarios (field rename, missing optional field, enum addition, numeric sent as string, extra fields, truncated arrays, nested object moved to top-level, timestamp in ms vs s).
3) Dashboard shows decoder success rate, reconciliation rate, quarantine rate, latency p95 < 120ms, and consumer lag.
4) Quarantine UI can show samples and create tickets with single-click link to a Drive-based incident template.
5) No customer traffic is dropped in production during rollout; default behavior is best-effort normalization with quarantine for failures tagged as "hard-reject".
implementation_notes:
Architecture: lightweight stateless Go service behind autoscaling group. Core components:
- Envelope normalizer: extracts standard headers and enriches with region and inferred SDK version.
- Schema registry client: reads schemas and reconciliation rules (backwards/forwards compatibility hints). Cache TTL 60s with SDS refresh.
- Reconciler engine: rule-based transformers (rename rules, type coercion, enum fallback mapping) and a sandboxed JS expression runner for customer-specific fixes.
- Validator: fast schema check (compiled JSON Schema + custom validators for rate-limited fields).
- Router: forward-to-canonical OR quarantine topic; attach provenance metadata (decoder_version, reconciliation_steps, trace_id).

Backpressure & throughput: consumer uses Kafka consumer group with partition parallelism; implement backpressure by examining consumer lag and throttling checkpoint commits. We'll use adaptive batching for high-throughput bursts (configurable max_batch_bytes) to keep p95 low.

Schema registry: start with Confluent-compatible registry adapters; store reconciliation rules in Git-backed config (docs/schema-reconciler/). Reconciliation rules versioned per-model.

Idempotency: emit deterministic event_id using sha256(canonical_payload + source_offset) so downstream dedup can operate.

Security: decoder runs in VPC, uses KMS for keys when contacting registry; logs redact PII fields per policy.

Rollout: gradual canary by customer shard (10% -> 30% -> 100%), with automatic fallback to pass-through forwarding if quarantine spike > 2% for >15m.
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Design review with PM and Observability. Agreed on quarantine topic and UI prototype. Action: engineering to produce data contract for 8 drift cases.

2025-02-18: Spike completed for JS sandbox and reconciler rules. Found that sandbox adds ~8ms, moved to async enrichment where possible. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4823
2025-02-24: End-to-end staging pipeline validated with synthetic traffic generator. Quarantine rate at 0.6% for staged schema drift tests. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/usage/decoder-health
2025-03-01: Canary deployment started for shard 'eu-west-1-a' (10% traffic). Observability alerts configured; on-call rotation updated.
qa_plan: Create a test harness that replays historical raw events with injected drift patterns. Run gated E2E tests in staging that assert canonical payload schema and monitor quarantine rates. QA to verify that PII redaction rules fire for 6 sample event types. Load test to 2x current peak throughput and ensure p95 latency < 120ms. Acceptance tests in CI must include schema-registry failure simulation (503) and validate graceful pass-through behavior.
monitoring_playbook: Primary dashboards: decoder success rate, reconciliation rate, quarantine rate, consumer lag, p95/p99 latency. Alerts: quarantine rate >1% sustained for 10m (sev3), consumer lag > 5k messages for 5m (sev2), decoder error rate >0.5% (sev2). Runbook links to incident template and rollback instructions. On alert, first step: check decoder logs for reconciliation failures and sample quarantined messages. Escalate to infra if Kafka offsets stall.
rollback_plan: Immediate: switch customer shard traffic back to legacy pass-through consumer via routing flag in Kafka consumer controller. If rollback not possible, flip feature-flag 'decoder_enabled' to false which causes producers to bypass the decoder. Post-mortem required for any rollback event.
risks_and_mitigation:
1) Risk: Over-eager reconciliation could mask real regressions. Mitigation: conservative default rules, tagging of auto-fixed fields in metadata, and audit logs.
2) Risk: JS sandbox could become attack surface. Mitigation: runtime limits, restricted allowed libraries, and heavy input validation.
3) Risk: Quarantine backlog. Mitigation: retention TTL + auto-compact to sample at 10% if backlog > 100k.
4) Risk: Increased consumer latency under burst. Mitigation: adaptive batching + autoscaling + circuit-breaker to pass-through.
notes: This ticket complements ENG-20341 (ingest orchestrator) and should be coordinated with the telemetry SDK team to add lightweight provenance headers. Expect follow-up tickets for Quarantine operator UI and schema-rule authoring tool.
